description.text: Use this option if your screen is not pure green/blue causing parts of the foreground to be transparent. Pick the color from the foreground that is affected.
Error threshold used for correcting the background area. All alpha values below this point will be set to 0.

Controls how much of the chroma difference between the source image and the screen color will be used in order to correct the matte. Increasing this value will generate a matte that has less transparent areas in the foreground. Please note that increasing the chroma gain will generate harder edges.
Use this option to remove remaining spill from around the foreground. One should use preferably skin tones and hair colors.
inside mask
Enable this option in order to define a despill bias that is different from the alpha bias.
Premultiplies the generated matte with the foreground to remove the screen.
replace mode
Adds the replace color into areas that the matte was corrected using black and white point. This can be enabled in order to enhance the despill effect.
Controls the amount of replace color to be added in the final result.
The color to add to the region of the matte that the above chosen mode specifies.

Defines the balance between the two non-primary components of the screen color. A balance close to 0 will bias the comparison towards the larger of the two, while a balance close to 1 will bias it towards the smaller component. A Screen Balance of 0.5 will treat the two non-primary components equally.
The screen color to make transparent.
Controls how much of the screen color will be used to define the foreground matte. Increasing this value will key more.
view
Error threshold used for correcting the foreground area. All alpha values above this point will be set to 1.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

description.plain_text: ChromaKeyer: Green and blue screen keyer. It was developed for use as a soft effect in Nuke Studio's timeline environment. Furthermore, it can take advantage of modern GPUs and multicore CPUs to accelerate the keying process when used for compositing. Use the screen color selector to determine the green/blue color from the source's screen. Adjust the intensity of the keying using the screen gain slider. Easily correct the generated matte by setting the white and black points of the matte. ChromaKeyer also provides the ability to fine-tune the keying result by setting a color that was wrongly made transparent to be the bias for the alpha. Moreover an inside mask can be used to add up the results of previous keying. In order to fine tune the despill results, despill bias can be set independenly from alpha. A replace color can be set to replace the background color, or to add on the edges and contribute on their smoothness. Finally, the generated alpha can be premultiplied with the rgb values.
description.text:
ChromaKeyer: Green and blue screen keyer. It was developed for use as a soft effect in Nuke Studio's timeline environment. Furthermore, it can take advantage of modern GPUs and multicore CPUs to accelerate the keying process when used for compositing.

Use the screen color selector to determine the green/blue color from the source's screen. Adjust the intensity of the keying using the screen gain slider. Easily correct the generated matte by setting the white and black points of the matte.

ChromaKeyer also provides the ability to fine-tune the keying result by setting a color that was wrongly made transparent to be the bias for the alpha. Moreover an inside mask can be used to add up the results of previous keying.

In order to fine tune the despill results, despill bias can be set independenly from alpha. A replace color can be set to replace the background color, or to add on the edges and contribute on their smoothness. Finally, the generated alpha can be premultiplied with the rgb values.
